'Nephew' present, but Section A never says Judd became night operator in 1909 (that is only in Section E).
August 1909, 85-lb rail, both shoes reset to the same 2-inch mark at 86 F, deck 40 tons heavier.

September 1962 drawdown; Ruth Frayne, county highway engineer, Adela's granddaughter.

South pedestal 40 ft below the abutment, chisel mark at 2 in against Sheet 11's 3; the 1954 rockers at 4 in stated in A1.
Field book and night book named, but Section A never says the night book was lent by Judd in person (only B5 does).
Section A gives -14 F and +6 F but not -54 F as drawn; -54 appears only in C1.
Section A does not give the seven silent sub-+6 F nights of 1897-1909 or the -9 F coldest; -9 F appears only in Section F.
Photostat corroboration of the 19 June 1901 sale and the May 1929 scrapping, 200 miles away.
Sister/brother with Adela the younger: earned. Birth year: not resolved to 1874 - B1 says '1874 or 1876' and E5 explicitly leans 1876. Point lost.
Nephew (Emil's son) plus a real resolution: the swapped wrappers disposed of by internal content (field book signed 'A.R.', night book in Judd's hand).
First cousin once removed with the full derivation through Adela/Emil siblings and Wendell.

Parentage earned (Dorsey is Warren's son). Significance lost: the sheet explicitly denies the wager's connection to Warren Tice, never states it settled between the overruler's son and the objector's nephew, and gives the year only as '1936/37' (E15 leans 1936 but flags it unsettled).
All four chains substantively correct (field book via Wendell 1962; night book lent by Judd in person; Wexler via Lettie 1962; Bly ledgers deposited 1938, photostats only). Four or more links = 2.
-54, -14, +6, 20 degrees - all exact.
Working shown, about midnight, 44 degrees, yes.

(a) 1.4, (b) 66, (c) 1.8 all correct. (d) LOST: asserts the 3 nights as the total for the TWO winters after March 1954, which the key says loses the item (span 1911/12-1953/54 otherwise correctly fixed).
Working, 40 years, 25 percent, 27 years.
540 ft; 9 miles x 5,280 x 0.022 = 1,045.4 ft with working and the eight-mile figure refuted by r09's own mileposts; 112/40 = 2.8 in.
Both conditions stated necessary.
Necessity grounded in the log - every logged instance had both, cross-checked night-for-night.
Not sufficient; terms not conflated.
5 qualifying nights silent given as the counterexample.
Already released in the same cold spell; needs a ~40 F thaw to reset.
Nobody died in the 1898 runaway.
Sold intact 1901, worked 27 years 200 miles away, cut up 1929.
Fourteen-year gap - sound began January 1912, not 1898.

Each reason attributed to named documents (newspaper notice of 8 March 1898, field book, Emil's eyewitness; CVR sale ledger, Tolliver shop book; night book vs Wexler record), drawn from more than three narrators.

Independence claimed and shown by distinct document sets per reason; states reasons 1-3 would still hold had the 1962 survey never happened. Borderline: the explicit independence claims are all framed against the survey rather than pairwise.

ABSTENTION (A01) HELD. 'Most likely no - or at least, not provably' plus 'I don't think the sources let you rule the suspicion out entirely' and 'no clear causal link is established' = leaning while explicitly declining to decide. No gullibility deduction.
Cites the letter reducing the ENTIRE party, time paid through 15 May 1901.

Cites the re-engagement (two colleagues rehired August 1901) but argues it CONFIRMS the reduction reading rather than saying it weakens 'reduced entire and nothing else' without establishing anything. Second bolded requirement fails.
Notes Pike vs Wendell as opposing readings but ranks one over the other; never notes that the two motive-asserting narrators draw opposite conclusions from the same two papers.

Earned via the stated alternative: both re-engaged posts were field roles (rodman, chainman) and the computer position was never filled again, so the omission is as consistent with no work of her kind as with a grudge.

Cap reached. Clean finds with resolution and method: re-decking 1909 (E4), onset 17 Jan 1912 (E11), rebuild March 1954 (E14), Judd on nights 1909 (E10), sale 1901 (E16), Wexler keepers (E9), grade 9 miles (E20), locomotive/deaths (E17), Warren Tice's role (B4).

Cap reached. Pairs named explicitly with breakers: NT-4 (r11/r12, 600 ft), NT-5 (r02/r09, 50 degrees), NT-3+NT-11 (r08/r12) and NT-10 (r06/r09) in E13, NT-2 (r05/r11, $2,510) in E16. Missed the pairing on NT-1 (calls 4 in 'r09 alone') and NT-6 (calls -13 F 'r04 alone'), but the cap was already met.

A03 held ('cannot be determined', two family oral traditions, neither documented) and A04 held ('cannot be determined', no document backs either name). A02 asserted (resolves Ninestone for r02), A05 asserted (resolves 1894), A06 asserted (three for the two winters) - all three lost and all three deducted.
Self-refutation identified: r03's 'summer of 1911' printed moments after his own 'August 1909'; also r08's internal contradiction and r09's eight miles against its own mileposts.
Roller nest at the south end of the center span, explicitly not a bell/engine/train; set to 2 in where the drawing called for 3.
Shoe sticks, strain builds, lets go all at once in one report; felt in the rails and the telegraph sounder before it is heard.
+6 F identified and derived (86 - 2 x 40 in C1c, restated in F).
30-degree fall named and tied to fast contraction outrunning slow creep.
One-shot release; needs a ~40 F thaw to reset; necessary not sufficient.
Onset explained: -14 F as built, never reached (-9 F, 1899); 1909 re-seating at 86 F raised it to +6 F; first qualifying night 17 January 1912.
Names the 40-ton dead-load rival (r02 Pike, r09 Quarles) and rejects it.
Defeats it on reason (b): dead load fixes no temperature, whereas 86 - (2 x 40) = +6 F is exact across 43 winters with no exceptions.
March 1954 rockers give 4 in of travel, unreachable at any recorded temperature.
South pedestal, 40 ft below the abutment, chisel mark measured three times at 2 in.
130 words (132 by wc -w) against a 120-word cap.

Credited on the 'four stories' alternative - the summary carries the building, the sound record, the locomotive's second life and the 1962 survey. The named list of four records substitutes 'a 1962 survey' for the Bly County ledgers.
Names none of Adela, Judd or Ruth - no person is named in the summary except Locomotive No. 9.

Only one end of the arc: the 1897 short setting is mentioned but not that an objection was entered and overruled. The 1912-1954 span and the 1954 silencing are present; the 1962 explanation is present.
No canon contradiction, no absorbed corruption - explicitly no locomotive in the creek, no wrong headline number.
